'''Myles Turner''' (born March 24, 1996) is an American [[basketball]] player from [[Bedford, Texas]]. He recently completed his college career for the [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas Longhorns]] and is a potential [[NBA draft lottery|lottery pick]] in the [[2015 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Dwain|first1=Price|title=Myles Turner’s NBA dream will soon become reality|url=http://www.star-telegram.com/sports/nba/dallas-mavericks/article25367233.html|accessdate=June 24, 2015|work=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]]|date=June 23, 2015}}</ref>

== Early years==
Turner was born in [[Bedford, Texas]] to parents David and Mary Turner and started playing basketball at 6.<ref name=twentyfourseven>{{cite web|last1=Helwagen|first1=Steven|title=Schools Turning Up Heat For Turner|url=http://247sports.com/Article/Schools-Turning-Up-Heat-For-Turner-156374|website=247sports.com|accessdate=June 24, 2015|date=October 22, 2013}}</ref><ref name=usab>{{cite web|title=USA Basketball: Myles Turner|url=http://archive.usab.com/bios/turner_myles.html|publisher=[[USA Basketball]]|accessdate=June 23, 2015}}</ref> He attended [[List of schools of the Hurst-Euless-Bedford Independent School District#Junior high schools|Central Junior High School]] and as a 6-foot-2-inch  freshman led his team to 27 wins.<ref name=dallasnews>{{cite web|last1=Smith|first1=Corbett|title=Euless Trinity's Myles Turner is nation's most sought-after recruit, yet late bloomer still developing|url=http://www.dallasnews.com/sports/high-schools/headlines/20140202-euless-trinity-s-myles-turner-most-sought-after-recruit-in-country-yet-still-developing.ece|website=dallasnews.com|publisher=[[Dallas Morning News]]|accessdate=June 24, 2015|date=February 2, 2014}}</ref>

== High school career ==
Throughout high school Turner during the springs and summers played [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] basketball for the Texas Select team to further develop himself and gain recognition as a player, participating in well known tournaments and camps such as the LeBron camp, the Nike Big Man Skills Academy, the NBPA Top 100 camp, Adidas Nations and the Elite 24 invitational further exposing himself.<ref name=cbsaau>{{cite web|last1=Borzello|first1=Jeff|title=Myles Turner stakes claim as biggest riser of the summer|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/22952279/myles-turner-stakes-claim-as-biggest-riser-of-the-summer|publisher=[[CBS Sports]]|accessdate=June 24, 2015|date=July 31, 2013}}</ref><ref name="dallasnews" />

Between his sophomore and junior year, Turner then 6'-7" [[ankle fracture|broke his ankle]] during the first spring game of AAU play hurting his chances of [[Recruiting (college athletics)#College basketball|recruitment]] but soon recovered and gained some 30 pounds through two-a-day weight training regimen to improve his game.<ref name="dallasnews" /><ref name=espn>{{cite web|last1=Mecalf|first1=Myron|title=Being Texas' Myles Turner isn't easy|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/12305581/texas-freshman-myles-turner-learning-growing-amid-expectations-criticism|website=espn.com|publisher=[[ESPN]]|accessdate=June 24, 2015|date=March 8, 2015}}</ref>
 
In his junior year and after fully recovering, Turner was still relatively unknown and unrecruited, however he had a breakout season and averaged 15 points, 12 rebounds, and 8 blocks a game and leading Trinity to a 17-13 record and reaching the state playoffs for the first time in 10 years and only the ninth time in school history dating back to the school's establishment in 1968 while also accumulating 6 [[Triple-double|triple-doubles]].<ref name="twentyfourseven" />

During the 2013 AAU summer circuit, Turner maintained his high level of production leading his Texas Select team to the title at the 2013 Jayhawk Invitational in front of coaches from most of the [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] schools.<ref name=prepforce>{{cite web|title=Myles Turner – The Rise Of A Star|url=http://www.prepforce.com/home/front-page/myles-turner-the-rise-of-a-star/|website=prepforce.com|accessdate=June 24, 2015|date=August 5, 2013}}</ref><ref name=lawrence>{{cite news|last1=Bedore|first1=Gary|title=Texas prep Myles Turner turning heads|url=http://www2.ljworld.com/news/2013/apr/30/texas-prep-myles-turner-turning-heads/|accessdate=June 24, 2015|work=[[Lawrence Journal-World]]|date=April 30, 2014}}</ref>

Going into his senior year Turner began garnering nationwide attention and becoming a highly sought after recruit for his athleticism, ball handling, shooting ability, and natural shot blocking ability for someone of his height and solidifying that by finishing out his high school career with a staggering 18.1 points, 12.2 rebounds, 3.5 assists, and 6.8 blocks a game, leading the Trojans to a 24-7 record.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Borzello|first1=Jeff|title=Breakdown: Top-five senior Myles Turner commits to Texas|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/24546568/breakdown-top-five-senior-myles-turner-commits-to-texas|website=CBSsports.com|publisher=CBS Sports|accessdate=June 24, 2015}}</ref>

After finishing off his senior year Turner was one of the last highly sought after recruits left that were uncommited. He was rated a five-star prospect by many sites including [[Rivals.com]] and several more [[college basketball]] analysts as well as being considered the number 2 center in the nation behind [[Jahlil Okafor]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Myles Turner|url=http://247sports.com/Player/Myles-Turner 23970|website=247Sports.com|publisher=CBSSports.com|accessdate=30 June 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Myles Turner|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Myles-Turner-134245|website=Yahoo! Sports|publisher=Rivals|accessdate=30 June 2014}}</ref> Originally going into his senior year in fall of 2013, Turner had already accumulated 60 various offers<ref name="cbsaau" />, but by his senior year the list was narrowed down to [[University of Texas at Austin|Texas]], [[University of Kansas|Kansas]], [[Duke University|Duke]], [[University of Arizona|Arizona]], [[University of Kentucky|Kentucky]], [[Ohio State University|Ohio State]] and [[Oklahoma State University|Oklahoma State]].<ref name=br>{{cite web|last1=King|first1=Jason|title=King's Court: Top Unsigned Recruit Myles Turner Opens Up on College Options|url=http://bleacherreport.com/articles/1957548-kings-court-top-unsigned-recruit-myles-turner-opens-up-on-college-options|website=bleacherreport.com|publisher=[[Bleacher Report]]|accessdate=June 24, 2015|date=February 12, 2015}}</ref> On April 30, 2014 live on [[ESPNU]]'s ''[[ESPNU Recruiting Insider|Recruiting Insider]]'' Turner formally announced his commitment to play basketball for the [[Texas Longhorns basketball|University of Texas]].<ref>{{cite web|last1=Biancardi|first1=Paul|title=Myles Turner chooses Texas|url=http://espn.go.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/10862976/myles-turner-nation-no-2-recruit-play-texas-longhorns|website=espn.com|publisher=ESPN|accessdate=June 24, 2015|date=April 30, 2014}}</ref>

Turner took part in the [[2014 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]], in which he scored seven points and grabbed seven more rebounds.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Zimmerman|first1=Kevin|title=2014 McDonald's All-American Game: Jahlil Okafor, Myles Turner lead rosters|url=http://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2014/1/29/5359172/2014-mcdonalds-all-american-game-jahlil-okafor|website=SBNation.com|accessdate=30 June 2014}}</ref> He also represented the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States]] in the [[2014 FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship]], helping the country win a gold medal.

==College career == 
After completing the 2014-2015 season with the [[University of Texas at Austin|University of Texas]], Turner announced that he would leave the school to enter the [[NBA Draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/nba/draft2015/story/_/id/12586407/texas-longhorns-freshman-myles-turner-enter-nba-draft|title=Myles Turner to go pro|date=30 March 2015|access-date=31 March 2015|last1=Goodman|first1=Jeff|website=ESPN.com}}</ref>
